articles.title: Aion UT: Chinese EV to rival Volkswagen ID 3 from under £30k
articles.title_tr: Aion UT: Chinese EV to rival Volkswagen ID 3 from under £30k
articles.summary:
"China's version of the Mini" looks to offer Brits more kit than other electric hatchbacks for similar money

Chinese newcomer Aion will challenge the Volkswagen ID 3 and MG 4 EV with the UT, an electric hatchback priced from less than £30,000.
Due in showrooms from October, it officially offers 268 miles of range and can be charged from 30-80% in 24 minutes.
It's powered by a front-mounted electric motor with 204bhp, giving a 0-62mph dash time of 7.3sec.
Designed in Milan, Italy, the UT is slightly longer and wider than the ID 3, owing to Chinese buyers’ demands for interior space.
GAC-owned Aion has previously described it as “China’s version of the Mini”, owing to its small footprint and upmarket aspirations.
As with the larger Aion V SUV (the brand’s debut model in the UK), the interior goes big on digital touchpoints, with a 14.6in infotainment touchscreen and an 8.8in instrument display.

In Chinese-market examples, the front seats can be folded flat to form a bed-like arrangement with the rear bench – although it remains to be seen whether this functionality will be offered in the UK. 
Aion claims the UT will offer “high-quality materials” for the class. For example, its windowsills are moulded to give the impression of stitched leather, despite being plastic, while the backing of the doorcards has a geometric finish that mimics carbonfibre.
The UT will be offered in a single trim level, but there will be an optional package that adds luxuries such as ventilated front seats, a panoramic glass roof and a powered tailgate.
Aion said it has tweaked the UT’s chassis to suit pockmarked British roads, creating a different set-up for the springs, dampers, bump-stops and anti-roll bar compared with European and Chinese examples.

articles.title: Jaguar's next-gen interior stays true to 'copy nothing' promise
articles.title_tr: Jaguar's next-gen interior stays true to 'copy nothing' promise
articles.summary:
Classy, richly-appointed interior is a statement for the brand, showcasing a new take on luxury

The arrival of the new Jaguar Type 01 interior pictures created one of those ‘everyone around the laptop’ moments in the office to have a look when they landed.
The reaction as we opened the files for the first time? Muted appreciation. No dropped jaws. Lots of ‘ahhh yeahs’ and ‘oooookays’.
In reality, nothing was ever going to top the unveiling of the original concept car almost two years ago, one whose exterior was so dramatic and shocking that we actually had to remind ourselves whether Jaguar did ever show pictures of the interior. It did, and the production version stays true to it. 
The Type 01’s interior looks classy, upmarket and almost Scandinavian in its use of light and materials. It’s a world away from the Jaguars we’ve come to know in modern times but also just as far away from anything bearing the Range Rover brand. Jaguar is very much going to do its own thing, and these pictures show it. 

The Type 00 concept made such a statement that Jaguar could only double down on that for production. To do any less or water it down would have undermined the very essence of the project.
Given the close visual relationship between the concept and production interiors, the same will be true for the exterior and those proportions. Jaguar has told us as much.
The interior was such a small part of the story then – as it was always going to be, with that styling and those proportions on the outside – but will become a far more important one in production. It isn’t showy and demonstrates a different way of being classy beyond anything high-tech or more traditional in its take on luxury. 
It’s to Jaguar’s credit that this car makes as big a visual statement now as it did when we first saw it in December 2024, and it’s the design that lives long in the memory after the whole ‘woke’ rebrand campaign furore around it has been forgotten.
It has been a long time coming, the new Jaguar. Too long. Getting here has been messy. Mistakes have been made, things have been said that can’t be unsaid. But at the end of it all does come a tangible reinvention for the brand, something different and a chance for success. 
We’re now only weeks away from seeing the finished thing.

articles.title: Jaguar Type 01 interior revealed - luxury GT majors on "hidden" tech
articles.title_tr: Jaguar Type 01 interior revealed - luxury GT majors on "hidden" tech
articles.summary:
Sleek production interior of the new-era electric GT is unveiled ahead of car's full reveal in October

Jaguar has revealed the bold interior of the new Type 01 electric GT ahead of the car's full unveiling in October.
The new four-seater will kick-start the British brand's reinvention as an all-electric luxury marque. But while prototypes of the Type 01 have been seen testing extensively - and been driven by Autocar - this is the first time Jaguar has shown any of the car without camouflage.
The interior takes clear inspiration from that of the controversial Type 00 concept and the firm calls it "a concept car vision brought to production".
Read more | Opinion: Jaguar's next-gen interior stays true to 'copy nothing' promise
The most notable feature of the design is a large 'central spine' - termed a "signature art piece" by Jaguar - that runs the entire length of the cabin between both the front and rear seats.
The spine divides the interior into four sections, each with its own individual seat. One of the images also confirms that the Type 01 has a low, swooping ceiling that features panoramic glass.

The driving position appears to be low-set and the dashboard is notably clear of instrumentation. There is a large digital information display screen in front of the driver, but only a small touchscreen console for heating and infotainment controls rising from the central spine. Jaguar refers to this as "hidden on-demand technology", which, it claims, has been integrated directly into the car's architecture.
There is also a distinct division between the driver and front passenger sections in the design of the dashboard.
An overhead image shows that the 'strikethrough' motifs on the dashboard also appear on the top lip of the bonnet in an attempt to fuse the interior and exterior design.
Another notable feature is that the car lacks a traditional rear-view mirror - the images also confirm that, like the Polestar 4, the Type 01 will not have a rear window - but instead has a digital rear-view camera. Unusually, the screen for this is located at the base of the windscreen, matched to the height of the wing mirrors.
Jaguar cites travertine stone and "the rich textures of artisan textiles" as influences for the cabin, with select elements chosen to add to the premium feel, such as the brass-inspired finish of the central spine and top of the doors, which feature Jaguar's leaper logo embossed into them.

Jaguar boss Rawdon Glover called the Type 01 "unmistakable from every angle", adding that it "has an interior like no other".
The Type 01 will be shown at Monterey Car Week in California this weekend in a new camouflage wrap. Its unveiling is scheduled for 6 October in New York.

articles.title: Vauxhall Astra driven: is the PHEV the pick of the line-up?
articles.title_tr: Vauxhall Astra driven: is the PHEV the pick of the line-up?
articles.summary:
Plug-in hybrid version of British family stalwart gets a fresh look and a longer electric-only range

When price is largely removed as a factor, choosing a powertrain becomes a matter of personal preference and use case – putting the power in the buyer's hands.That's what Vauxhall has done with the revamped Astra for this mid-life facelift: the hybrid, plug-in hybrid and electric versions of the Volkswagen Golf rival all start at the same price, regardless whether you choose the hatchback or Sports Tourer estate body.Given the industry trend, that might prompt many buyers to look towards the EV, which we've reviewed separately, but there are plenty of buyers who aren't ready to make that leap yet, for all manner of reasons. And for those reasons, the PHEV version feels like it could be the sweet spot in the line-up for many, offering genuinely useful real-world electric running with the convenience of a combustion engine.

articles.title: Vauxhall Astra Electric Sports Tourer review: more range for UK stalwart
articles.title_tr: Vauxhall Astra Electric Sports Tourer review: more range for UK stalwart
articles.summary:
Quiet British success story continues with a fresh look and bigger battery for EV version

The Vauxhall Astra is one of the UK’s best-selling cars of recent years, racking up more than three million sales across 46 years and eight generations. Yet it often feels a bit underappreciated. It’s hard to imagine the Astra’s demise would garner the same coverage granted that of its shorter-lived rival, the Ford Focus.But it should be celebrated, because this longtime Volkswagen Golf rival is still going strong, battling valiantly against SUV hegemony. It has just received a mid-life update and now offers a more extensive line-up than ever: you can pick either a hatchback or Sports Tourer estate body and pure-petrol, hybrid, plug-in hybrid or fully electric power.Vauxhall has made much of offering pricing parity across both bodystyles and the three electrified powertrains (the pure petrol remains the cheapest), but that’s a bit deceptive: thanks to the UK government's Electric Car Grant, the EV is actually £1500 cheaper than either the hybrid or PHEV even before you account for lower first year VED and BIK rates.All this makes this Astra Sports Tourer Electric a bit of a bargain, even in top-spec £32,495 Ultimate trim tested here (an entry-level Griffin will set you back £28,495).
